append_only: Fields of this pre-registration are never edited after commit to main. Corrections and clarifications are appended to amendments[] with a date and reason, before any VAL inference they could affect. A changed model, prompt, decoding, metric, sample, sharding rule or comparator is a new plan_id, not an amendment. An activated copy may differ from this file only in activated, activation and status; the runner compares every other field with the committed plan and refuses any difference.

generation.generation_config_override_reason: The pinned Qwen2.5-VL-3B generation_config.json sets repetition_penalty 1.05, which Backend.predict would apply under greedy decoding and which penalises copying label tokens that appear in the prompt's allowed list. The endpoints' base config (Qwen2-VL-2B @895c3a49) has repetition_penalty 1.0. Overriding to 1.0 makes decoding pure greedy, equal to the endpoints. Chosen before any inference.

cpu_numerics.reason: PR plumbing run 39110248770 landed on an AMD EPYC 9V45 (native avx512_bf16) and answered 'DC-8' for TRAIN image 0056978, where four runs on AVX2-class hosts (one recorded as AMD EPYC 7763) answered 'Global Express'; it was also ~30x faster (9.4 s per image). So with default kernels the bf16 outputs depend on the host a shard lands on. The runner sets ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY=avx2 before torch is imported, disables oneDNN (torch.backends.mkldnn.enabled = False), and refuses unless torch reports capability AVX2 with oneDNN off; both values are in every shard identity, so the merge refuses a mix. Whether this equalises the 9V45's answers is checked by the plumbing canary (stages.plumbing.expected_responses) on every PR, not assumed.

gate.requires: A committed discovery receipt (discovery-receipt.json from a merged discovery run) passed as the dispatch input discovery_receipt. It must carry this activated plan's SHA256, status completed, the pre-registered discovery ids_sha256, all 100 images completed of 100, one first-attempt run on refs/heads/main, an identity whose plan_sha256, stage, run_id and sha match the receipt, and the same runner_sha256 and workflow_sha256 as the checkout dispatching full VAL.
gate.shard_rule: N >= ceil(3333 / floor((shard_wall_seconds - image_seconds - discovery max_fixed_setup_seconds) / max(330, 3.0 x (discovery max_shard_mean_image_latency_seconds + discovery mean_image_fetch_seconds)))). max_shard_mean_image_latency_seconds is the largest of the four discovery shards' mean generation latencies. fixed setup = a shard's setup seconds minus its image-fetch seconds (frozen import, model download and rehash, load); fetch seconds are charged per image because a full shard fetches all its images during setup. The matrix command refuses a smaller N, and refuses a receipt whose timing values are not positive numbers.
gate.on_stop: Report the named comparator as incomplete. Do not change prompt, decoding, model, sample or comparators to rescue it.
gate.latency_safety_factor_basis: Measured runner-to-runner spread on identical free ubuntu-24.04 runners (4 vCPU, 16 GB): plumbing means 113.07 s (run 39105775526) and 297.80 / 297.87 s (runs 39106885360, 39106233184) per image, a 2.63x ratio, with identical responses. 3.0 is above that ratio, so shards sized from an all-fast discovery still fit a slow host: budget max(330, 3.0 x (113.07 + 1.1)) = 342.5 s gives floor(18835 / 342.5) = 54 images, and 54 x (297.8 + 1.1) s + 65 s = 16,206 s, inside the 18,900 s start limit. Under the pinned kernel path the measured spread is 2.89x (297.35 s on an EPYC 7763, 102.98 s on an EPYC 9V45); a discovery all on 9V45 hosts gets the 330 s floor (3.0 x (102.98 + 1.1) = 312.2 s), 57 images, and 57 x (297.35 + 1.1) s + 65 s = 17,077 s, still inside the limit.
gate.latency_floor_basis: About 1.1x the slowest per-image mean measured on a free runner (297.9 s plus ~1 s fetch), so a discovery on fast hosts never sizes shards below what a slow host needs: 57 images x 298.9 s + 65 s = 17,102 s, inside the 18,900 s start limit.
gate.on_slow_host: A host slower than the per-image budget (max of 330 s and 3.0x the slowest discovery shard) stops its shard as partial at the start rule; the merge refuses the run, which is reported under runs_policy and never patched. Each shard records host cpu_model and cpu_flags, and the receipt lists each shard's cpu_model and mean latency, so the spread can be attributed. CPU model is deliberately not part of the merge identity: shards of one run land on mixed hosts.

sharding.assignment: Stage image i in author order belongs to shard i mod N; each shard runs its images in author order.
sharding.dispatch_ref: refs/heads/main only. The workflow's setup job and the runner's shard and merge commands refuse any other ref, because a branch could edit the plan and the runner together and pass the activated-copy lock. Each shard identity records runner_sha256 and workflow_sha256.
sharding.start_rule: A shard starts an image only if its elapsed seconds plus image_seconds stay within shard_wall_seconds; otherwise it stops as partial, so no image is cut by the 6 h GitHub job limit.
sharding.stop_rule: A shard stops at its first generation error, interrupted image or budget stop and fails; nothing is retried or regenerated.
merge_refuses: any shard index in [0, N) without a completed shard record, or any unexpected artifact
any image missing, duplicated, out of its partition or outside the stage manifest; every image must be scored exactly once
any non-completed outcome (generation error, unknown after interruption, partial shard)
any shard from a re-run attempt (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT != 1), another workflow run or another commit
any shard whose model, runtime, profile, generation config, prompt or frozen-source identity differs from the others
any canonical label that differs from the frozen parser applied to the raw response
sharding.runs_policy: Every dispatched VAL run is reported, failed or not. A failed run is never patched by re-running shards; a new dispatch is a new run and the report lists it next to the failed one. The first run that merges is the result for its stage. Dispatched runs never cancel each other: the workflow's concurrency group is per run for workflow_dispatch.

analysis.metric: mean(diag(row_normalized_confusion)) via the frozen classification_comparison; micro accuracy supplemental
analysis.comparison_direction: compare_classification(gold, named_baseline, endpoint): candidate is the named baseline, comparator the endpoint, on all 3,333 images and the full vocabulary
analysis.endpoint_export_check: Before any baseline comparison, the merge recomputes compare_classification(gold, arm, common) for RL400 and the strongest SFT from the committed export with the frozen code and requires the full result (scores, per-class differences, bootstrap intervals, input_sha256) to equal versus_common_initialization[arm] in the committed report. The export was made by scripts/export_native_val_endpoint_predictions.py from the evaluator journals whose SHA256 the report records, and it reproduced both input_sha256 values at export time.
analysis.discovery_reporting: numerator, denominator, macro (= micro by balance), Hoeffding interval, valid fraction, unterminated answers, latency and setup seconds; no paired comparison on the 100-image sample
analysis.claim_limits: A named native-VAL baseline claim requires all 3,333 predictions with zero non-completed outcomes from one merged run. VAL was the selection set for the strongest SFT, so a comparison against it is a development comparison. Nothing here touches the frozen native TEST.

measured_cost.run_sha_note: artifact_run_sha is GITHUB_SHA of the pull_request run, i.e. GitHub's merge commit of the head into main at that time, not the head commit; both are given so the instrument can be re-located.
measured_cost.spread: Under default kernels: ~9.4 s per image on an AMD EPYC 9V45 (AVX-512 bf16), 113.07 s on one host whose CPU was not recorded, and 297.73-297.87 s on three others, one recorded as AMD EPYC 7763 (AVX2, no AVX-512). The 9V45 also changed one answer. Under the pinned AVX2 kernel path, with the canary answers in both: 297.35 s per image on an EPYC 7763 (run 39110959125) and 102.98 s on an EPYC 9V45 (run 39124326521), a 2.89x spread, still below the factor 3.0. The pinned path has not been measured on the unrecorded 113 s host; the latency floor and factor do not depend on it.
measured_cost.endpoint_export_check: verify-endpoints in each of these jobs: the frozen compare_classification reproduced versus_common_initialization for rl-exposure and sft-1e5-time exactly
measured_cost.projection_unverified: Three images per run are not a forecast. Full VAL generation is 3333 x 113 s = ~105 runner-hours to 3333 x 298 s = ~276 runner-hours on AVX2-class hosts, free on a public repository. The shard rule (floor 330 s, factor 3.0, fixed setup ~65 s) gives N = ceil(3333 / floor(18835 / 330)) = 59 shards whenever the slowest discovery shard averages under ~109 s, and ceil(3333 / floor(18835 / (3.0 x 298.9))) = 159 if it is slow; both are within the 256 maximum. The binding numbers come from the committed discovery receipt, not from this record.
